definitions.explanation: Rain that starts suddenly and usually stops after a short time. A brief, unexpected shower.

examples.japanese: {俄雨|にわかあめ}に{降|ふ}られて{濡|ぬ}れてしまった。
examples.english: I got caught in a sudden shower and got soaked.

examples.japanese: {午後|ごご}は{俄雨|にわかあめ}の{可能性|かのうせい}があります。
examples.english: There's a chance of sudden showers this afternoon.

examples.japanese: {俄雨|にわかあめ}が{止|や}むまで{軒下|のきした}で{待|ま}った。
examples.english: I waited under the eaves until the sudden shower stopped.

notes:
CHARACTERISTICS:
・Starts suddenly without much warning
・Usually stops after a short time
・Common in summer months in Japan

KANJI BREAKDOWN:
・{俄|にわか} (sudden, unexpected) + {雨|あめ} (rain)

RELATED WEATHER TERMS:
・{夕立|ゆうだち} (evening rain shower - specifically in summer, often with thunder)
・{通|とお}り{雨|あめ} (passing shower)
・ゲリラ{豪雨|ごうう} (guerrilla rainstorm - modern term for sudden heavy downpours)

WEATHER FORECAST EXPRESSION:
・{俄雨|にわかあめ}に{注意|ちゅうい} (beware of sudden showers)
・{所|ところ}により{俄雨|にわかあめ} (showers in some areas)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{俄雨|にわかあめ} is a common occurrence in Japanese summers, especially during the {梅雨|つゆ} (rainy season) and {夏|なつ}. Carrying a {折|お}りたたみ{傘|がさ} (folding umbrella) is standard practice in Japan.
